memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So God made the vault and separated the water under the vault from the water above it. And it was so. God called the vault "sky." And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day. - Gen 1:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
I've combined these two verses, since they complete one thought, God forming the vault and then naming it.

Here we see God carrying out exactly what He had just spoken. He said, "Let there be a vault," and now the verse tells us God made it, and "it was so." What God declares, God does. There is no gap between His word and His work. This is the kind of God we serve, utterly reliable, whose promises always come to pass.

God then names the vault "sky." Every time we look up at that vast blue expanse, we are looking at something God spoke into being and personally named. The ordinary sky above our heads is a daily reminder of His power and faithfulness.

Notice again the closing rhythm: "there was evening, and there was morning." Another full day of God's good work, ordered and complete. He finishes what He begins.

This steadies us. The God whose word never fails is the same God who has spoken over your life through His promises in Scripture. Not one of them will fall to the ground. In Christ, every promise of God finds its "Yes" (2 Cor 1:20). So when God says something, you can build your life on it, just as surely as the sky stands stretched above you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you truly believe that what God says, He will do?
2. When you look at the sky, does it stir wonder and trust in you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, what You speak, You always accomplish. Help me rest on Your unfailing word and trust every promise You have made. Amen.
